openings.claim: Small manual taps through an offset head and pin-only guide might align the pin; the guide is predicted to constrain contact and unintended side force.
openings.discriminator: Housing contact or an immobile pin defeats adequacy; no comparative vibration reduction is claimed.
openings.probe: Proposed only: inspect a surrogate contact envelope, then attempt incremental alignment under varied friction.
openings.uncertainty: Guide clearance, required impulse, and friction remain unknown; no alignment or damage result exists.

openings.claim: A controlled powered pulse head might reduce operator-dependent impulse variation compared with manual tapping.
openings.discriminator: Equal pulse variation defeats its proposed advantage; lower housing damage is not predicted.
openings.probe: Proposed only after explicitly relaxing manual-only actuation and establishing an actuator resource.
openings.uncertainty: Constraint relaxation is required; actuator availability and vibration transmission are unknown.

lineage.reason: Retains the manual pin-only alignment proposal and its adequacy limits.
Retains the distinct pulse-variation proposal as conditional and currently ineligible.

Violates no lubricant addition. Lower sliding resistance might reduce required impulse, but unspecified friction could yield no effect; contamination and compatibility remain unresolved. No trial is proposed.

decision: D1 is the current constraint-compatible proposal for moving the pin to its reference mark without housing damage. Enforce no housing contact, no lubricant addition, and manual-only actuation. D2 requires an explicit change of scope; lubrication is excluded. All proposals are synthetic and untested: geometry and reference are hypothetical, friction unspecified, and no pin, housing, vibration measurements, usable equipment, or power source is supplied.
